name: Question 10
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨1-{e}^{t/2},3⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨0,1⟩$ when $t=2,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=0.$
worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨1-{e}^{t/2},3⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (1-{e}^{t/2})\,\text{d}t,\int 3\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨t-2{e}^{t/2}+{C}_{1},3t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(2)=⟨0,1⟩.$ Substituting $t=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =⟨2-2{e}^{2/2}+{C}_{1},3(2)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,1⟩ & =⟨2-2e+{C}_{1},6+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=2e-2$ and ${C}_{2}=-5.$ Therefore, the velocity is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨t-2{e}^{t/2}+2e-2,3t-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at time $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨0-2{e}^{0/2}+2e-2,3(0)-5⟩ \\  & =⟨2e-4,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

The acceleration a at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by a(t)=⟨1−et/2,3⟩. Given that the particle has velocity v=⟨0,1⟩ when t=2, calculate the velocity vector of P at time t=0.

a
v(0)=⟨e−4e,1⟩
b
v(0)=⟨2e−4,1⟩
c
v(0)=⟨e−1,−5⟩
d
v(0)=⟨e−4e,−3⟩
e
v(0)=⟨2e−4,−5⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨1−et/2,3⟩dt=⟨∫(1−et/2)dt,∫3dt⟩=⟨t−2et/2+C1,3t+C2⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(2)=⟨0,1⟩. Substituting t=2, we get v(2)=⟨2−2e2/2+C1,3(2)+C2⟩⟨0,1⟩=⟨2−2e+C1,6+C2⟩, so we must have C1=2e−2 and C2=−5. Therefore, the velocity is given by v(t)=⟨t−2et/2+2e−2,3t−5⟩.

Finally, the velocity at time t=0 is v(0)=⟨0−2e0/2+2e−2,3(0)−5⟩=⟨2e−4,−5⟩.
